column5: Evidence type clinical_study: a dose-escalation trial in pulmonary TB showed 360 mg SR every 12 h with rifampin reaches safe exposures, and the abstract cites efflux-pump inhibition and limited Mtb growth in macrophages.

Evidence type human_subject: a 7-patient case series of HIV-TB IRIS reported favorable outcomes at 100 mg/day with no adverse effects. It is uncontrolled and covers immunomodulation in IRIS, not bacterial killing.
Evidence type animal: it’s about a cat (no not our kat), it has no TB or HDT content.
Evidence type in_vitro: vorinostat (SAHA) added activity to rifampicin and lowered intracellular Mtb CFU in THP-1 macrophages. Valproic acid did better, and this is cell-culture data only.
Evidence type animal: a zebrafish–M. marinum screen found clemastine limits infection by potentiating P2RX7. It also worked in a granuloma explant model.

Evidence type other (in vitro macrophage study): flunarizine was the only one of 4 calcium modulators that enhanced macrophage killing of Mtb, through CaM–pCaMKII-dependent phagosome maturation. The authors call it an HDT candidate.
Evidence type animal: amiodarone inhibited intracellular Mtb and M. avium in primary human macrophages by inducing autophagy, and cut bacterial burden in zebrafish.

Evidence type animal: in zebrafish–M. marinum, atovaquone and pyrimethamine restored vascular barrier function without impairing innate control. Pyrimethamine is the paper's focus, and atovaquone's own anti-mycobacterial effect is not shown.
Evidence type other: It shows no host-cell or in vivo TB activity for coumarin.
Evidence type human_subject: etoposide is only the standard comparator and TB is one of several triggers. It gives no support for etoposide as a TB HDT.

Evidence type in_vitro: fluspirilene and pimozide inhibited intracellular Mtb, including MDR strains, in human macrophages through autophagy and lysosomal modulation. The authors call them translatable HDT candidates.
Evidence type human_subject: TB is only mentioned in passing, and itraconazole is the antifungal, not the HDT.
